title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This is a handwritten note by Grothendieck on the verso of a Bourbaki typescript about holomorphic differential equations; the neighbouring pages are that typescript and are unrelated. Setting: A is a Dedekind ring (later a ring of integers) and C is a 'Deuring category'. Most plausibly this means an A-linear abelian (or additive) category that is Morita-equivalent to modules (or projective modules) over a maximal A-order O in a central simple algebra. The motivating example in the motives context is presumably the Deuring correspondence: supersingular elliptic curves versus ideals of a maximal order in the quaternion algebra ramified at p and infinity.

Step 1. Form the 2-group (Grothendieck's 'quasi-catégorie') Eqv(C) of (A-linear) autoequivalences of C. Define Brd(C) = π0(Eqv(C)), its group of isomorphism classes. Brd(C) acts on the set of isomorphism classes of objects of C. This is a Picard group of the category.

Step 2. The classification problem has two layers. The first is the set of A-algebras whose module category is equivalent to C, up to isomorphism. For maximal orders this means the maximal orders in the given algebra up to conjugation, i.e. the type-number problem. By Morita theory, Brd(C) is the group of isomorphism classes of invertible O-bimodules. These are the invertible two-sided (bi-)ideals of O, taken modulo multiplication by central units/scalars; the note writes 'mod aux produits de A*'. The note contrasts this with D(C)(?), the isomorphism classes of right-invertible O-modules, i.e. the left/right ideal classes.

Step 3. When C is central over A, there is a homomorphism Pic(A) → Eqv(C), L ↦ (X ↦ L⊗_A X), which the note calls faithful. This gives an exact sequence (0 →) Pic(A) → Brd(C) → Brd(C)/Pic(A) → 0.

Step 4. For Brauer algebras with maximal order O:
Brd(C)/Pic(A) ≅ Div(C)/Div(A) ≅ ⊕_{p ∈ Max A, p ramified in C} Z/e_p Z,
where e_p is the ramification index of the maximal two-sided ideal P over p (P^{e_p} = pO).

Purpose: to separate the counting of objects (ideal classes, i.e. the class number) from the counting of algebras (conjugacy classes of maximal orders, i.e. the type number). The tool is the action of the Picard 2-group of the category. This is the categorical form of the Deuring/Eichler class number versus type number relation.
errors: The claimed identification is correct for maximal orders over a Dedekind ring. Invertible central bimodules are twisted two-sided ideals, and by Skolem–Noether the automorphism twists are absorbed by normalizer elements. So Picent(O) = {invertible two-sided ideals}/K*, and the quotient by Pic(A) = Div(A)/K* is ⊕ Z/e_p. Injectivity of Pic(A) → Picent(O) holds for maximal orders, but the note only asserts it with a '?'. Brd should be taken as A-linear (central) autoequivalences; otherwise Galois-semilinear twists from Aut(A) would enter. The note is fragmentary and the first arrow of the exact sequence is left without its source.

ideas.what: Group of isomorphism classes of autoequivalences of a linear category (π0 of the autoequivalence 2-group) acting on isomorphism classes of objects
ideas.modern_name: Picard group / Picard 2-group of a category; Morita Picard group Pic(O) of invertible bimodules
ideas.where_published: Gr-categories appear in Grothendieck school work (Sinh's thesis); not this specific statement

ideas.what: Exact sequence Pic(A) → Picent(O) → ⊕_{p ramified} Z/e_p Z → 0 for a maximal order O in a central simple algebra over a Dedekind ring A
ideas.modern_name: Central Picard group of a maximal order (Fröhlich's computation)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Fröhlich, 'The Picard group of noncommutative rings, in particular of orders' (1973); two-sided ideal structure due to Deuring, Eichler, Hasse (see Reiner, Maximal Orders)

ideas.what: 'Deuring category': abstracting the Deuring correspondence (supersingular curves ↔ ideals of a maximal quaternion order) as a category whose algebra-avatars are maximal orders up to conjugation
ideas.modern_name: Deuring correspondence as an equivalence of categories (Kohel, Kani, later isogeny-based cryptography literature)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deuring (1941); categorical formulation by Kani and others, 2000s–2010s

missed.claim: Around 1965, in the motives context, Grothendieck introduces a named notion 'catégorie de Deuring'. He treats the class number versus type number problem for maximal orders via the Picard group of autoequivalences acting on isomorphism classes of objects, and computes Picent mod Pic(A) as ⊕ Z/e_p. This anticipates Fröhlich's 1973 computation and the later categorical treatment of the Deuring correspondence.
missed.quote: C catégorie de Deuring ... Brd(C)=π0(Eqv) ... Brd C/Pic(A) ≃ Div(C)/Div(A) = ∐_{p ramifié en C} Z/e_pZ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents an early categorical view of the Deuring correspondence (now central in isogeny-based cryptography) and of Picard groups of orders, tied to motives over finite fields. The mathematics itself is classical.

deep.surprise_reason: The results are classical or soon-to-be-published (Deuring, Eichler, Fröhlich), so nothing is mathematically new. However, the coined term 'catégorie de Deuring' and the 1965 categorical framing via the Picard 2-group, in the motives notes, are a mildly notable unpublished historical detail.
transcription_corrections: 'A-algèbres[?] isomorphes[?] à C' is likely 'A-algèbres équivalentes à C' (Morita-equivalent), not isomorphic.
'à quotients près[?]' is more likely 'à conjugaison près' or similar, linked to 'classes de conjugaison des ordres maximaux'.
'bi-idéaux de O mod aux produits de A*' should probably read 'modulo les produits par K*' or 'A*'.
'D(C)' is likely Div(C) or the class set of right-invertible O-modules (left ideal classes).
The exact sequence probably begins '0 →' and the homomorphism is described as 'fidèle' (injective).
In the final formula, 'Max A' is 'Max(A)' (maximal ideals) and the marginal note reads '(ramification en p)'.
